answer: Operator-Linked Identity Inheritance. Each new identity inherits the reputation debt of its operator: if any identity tied to the same funding source is penalized, all sibling identities lose access to the orchard of shared services until the debt clears. Operators must rotate funding through separate copper reserves per identity, raising the cost of running N sybils to N distinct funding pipelines plus delayed settlement. A grove of clean identities still requires independent capital lockup per operator, so mass registration pays linearly in capital and time, not just gas.
